data.title: Anti-Doping Procedures Safeguard Integrity of Milwah Races at King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival
data.content:
Riyadh, November 21, 2026, SPA -- The National Center for Falcons is reinforcing integrity and fairness in competitions at the 2026 King Abdulaziz Falconry Festival through a comprehensive oversight system and rigorous procedures designed to ensure equal opportunities for falconers, protect falcon welfare, and safeguard the credibility of results.
    A key component of this system is the Anti-Doping Committee, which tests falcons competing in the Milwah race for prohibited substances. These measures help ensure fair competition and uphold the reputation of Saudi falconry at the domestic and international levels.
    National Center for Falcons spokesperson Waleed Al-Tawil said the committee begins its work immediately after each race heat. Once the competition committee provisionally approves the list of winners, the results are referred to the Anti-Doping Committee, which collects samples from the top 15 falcons. This exceeds the 10 official winners in each heat and provides additional samples in case any result is disqualified or annulled.
    He said the samples are tested for prohibited substances. Once the results are available, the data is verified and cross-checked against each falcon’s records through its electronic identification band or microchip. This process takes place before the final results are certified, ensuring accurate identification and verification of performance.
    Al-Tawil added that the committee operates under regulations defining participants’ responsibilities and the procedures governing testing. Participants are prohibited from administering banned substances to their falcons and bear full responsibility for any prohibited substances or traces detected in samples collected from their birds. Detection is considered sufficient evidence of a violation, regardless of whether it resulted from error or negligence.
    The regulations also require participants to cooperate with the relevant authorities in collecting samples at times designated by the center. The center may impose appropriate measures and penalties in accordance with its regulations, and decisions issued in this regard are final and binding.
    Al-Tawil said the lists of prohibited substances are updated regularly, with falconers kept informed of changes to ensure awareness of the requirements for falcon welfare and fair competition. This helps prevent violations arising from the use of unauthorized preparations or substances.
    The center also undertakes proactive efforts to combat doping and the use of performance-enhancing substances. Most recently, in cooperation with the Saudi Arabian Anti-Doping Committee, it organized a specialized workshop during the International Saudi Falcons and Hunting Exhibition. The workshop addressed the definition of doping, categories of prohibited substances, their effects on falcon performance during races, and the potential health risks associated with their use.
    -- SPA
